He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. He attended [[Kalamazoo Central High School]] where he won the [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]]. He was part of the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 team]] that won the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] and reached the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|championship game]] of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. ==Early life== Livers was born on July 28, 1998, in [[Kalamazoo, Michigan]], to Angela and Morris Livers.{{cite web|title=4 Isaiah Livers|url=http://mgoblue.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=15234|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|access-date=March 13, 2018}} He started playing basketball at the age of five with his father in the driveway.{{cite web|first=Jared|last=Purcell|title=Michigan signee Isaiah Livers of Kalamazoo Central is 2017 Mr. Basketball|url=http://highschoolsports.mlive.com/news/article/-185104844948235807/michigan-signee-isaiah-livers-of-kalamazoo-central-is-2017-mr-basketball/|website=[[MLive.com]]|date=March 20, 2017|access-date=January 13, 2018}} Michigan began recruiting Livers in May 2016 and he made his official visit on July 28, earning an offer.{{cite web|first=Brendan F.|last=Quinn|title=Isaiah Livers, a 4-star 2017 forward from Kalamazoo Central, commits to Michigan|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2016/08/4-star_kalamazoo_central_forwa.html|website=[[MLive.com]]|date=August 7, Michigan.{{cite web|first=Mark|last=Snyder|title=New Michigan basketball commit Isaiah Livers says he's perfect fit|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2016/08/09/michigan-basketball-isaiah-livers/88448218/|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=August 9, 2016|access-date=January 13, 2018}} He was named 2017 Michigan [[Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]].{{cite web|first=Patrick|last=Nothaft|title=Kalamazoo Central's Isaiah Livers wins Michigan Gatorade Player of the Year 2018|access-date=April 3, 2018}} ===Sophomore season (2018–2019)=== [[File:Isaiah Livers (Michigan Wolverines men's basketball player) during December 4, 2018 game against Northwestern Wildcats at Welsh-Ryan Arena in Evanston, Illinois (2).jpg|thumb|upright|Livers for the [[2018–19 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2018–19 Wolverines]]]] On January 13, [[2018–19 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|the 2018–19 Wolverines team]] defeated [[2018–19 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]] to establish a school record for best start at 17–0 and tied the school's record 17-game win streak.{{cite web|title=No. 2 Michigan now 17-0 after 80-60 win over Northwestern|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082459 Interactive]]|date=January 13, 2019|access-date=January 14, 2019}} On February 28, 2019, Michigan defeated [[2018–19 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] 82–53. Livers made his first start of the season, replacing an injured [[Charles Matthews (basketball)|Charles Matthews]], and posted 12 points and 10 assists, for his first career double-double.{{cite web |title=No. 9 Michigan beats Nebraska 82-53 in home finale |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082468|work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 28, 2019|access-date=February 28, 2019}}{{cite web |first=Tom |last=Wyrot |title=Michigan Dominates from Start to Finish Against Nebraska on Senior Night|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/2/28/mens-basketball-michigan-dominates-from-start-to-finish-against-nebraska-on-senior-night.aspx |website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=February 28, 2019 |access-date=February 28, 2019}} On March 14, Michigan defeated [[2018–19 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]] 76–49 in the semifinals of the Big Ten tournament, as Livers posted a career-high 21 points.{{cite web|title=Livers scores 21, No. 10 Michigan pounds Minnesota 76-49|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401120738|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 16, 2019 |access-date=March 16, 2019}}{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|title=Wolverines Dominate Gophers, Advance to Big Ten tournament Title Game |url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/16/mens-basketball-wolverines-dominate-gophers-advance-to-big-ten-tournament-title-game.aspx |website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=March 16, 2019|access-date=March 16, 2019}} Livers' 42.6% (52/122) three point shooting percentage led the Big Ten Conference.{{cite web |title=2021-22 Men's Basketball Media Guide |url=https://bigten.org/documents/2021/11/5/2021_22_Men_s_Basketball_Media_Guide.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214005608/https://bigten.org/documents/2021/11/5/2021_22_Men_s_Basketball_Media_Guide.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 14, 2021 |website=BigTen.org |publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |access-date=April 25, 2022}} ===Junior season (2019–2020)=== On November 12, Michigan defeated [[2019–20 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]] 79–69 in the [[Gavitt Tipoff Games]] behind a then career-high 22 points from Livers.{{cite web|title=Strong second half lifts Michigan past Creighton 79-69|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166058|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 12, 2019|access-date=November 12, 2019}}{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|title=Livers' Career Night Leads Michigan Past Creighton|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/11/12/mens-basketball-livers-career-night-leads-michigan-past-creighton.aspx|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=November 12, 2019|access-date=November 12, 2019}} On November 22, Michigan defeated [[2019–20 Houston Baptist Huskies men's basketball team|Houston Baptist]] 111–68 behind a career-high 24 points by Livers. Michigan's 111 points were the most points scored in a game since a 112–64 victory over [[1997–98 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] in [[1997–98 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1998]].{{cite web|title=Livers scores 24, Michigan routs Houston Baptist, 111-68|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166090|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 22, 2019|access-date=November 22, 2019}}{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|title=Simpson's Career Night Leads Michigan to Rout of Houston Baptist|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/11/22/mens-basketball-simpsons-career-night-leads-michigan-to-rout-of-houston-baptist.aspx|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=November 22, 2019|access-date=November 22, 2019}} He suffered a groin injury on December 21 in a win over [[Presbyterian Blue Hose men's basketball|Presbyterian]].{{cite news|title=Michigan forward Isaiah Livers out indefinitely with groin injury|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28379234/michigan-forward-isaiah-livers-indefinitely-groin-injury|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 27, 2019|access-date=December 30, 2019}} He missed nine of the next 10 games before facing [[2019–20 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] on February 8.{{cite web|title=Livers returns, Michigan beats No. 16 Michigan State 77-68|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166214|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=February 8, 2020|access-date=February 9, 2020}} On February 16, Livers suffered an ankle injury against [[2019–20 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] and missed the following game against [[2019–20 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]]. In his return versus [[2019–20 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], Livers had 19 points, six rebounds, two blocks and a steal in a 71–63 victory.{{cite news|first=Orion|last=Sang|title=Michigan basketball crossing fingers that Isaiah Livers' injury streak is over|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/02/24/michigan-basketball-isaiah-livers-injury/4852612002/|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=February 24, 2020|access-date=February 28, 2020}} On March 5, Michigan defeated [[2019–20 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] 82–58, as Livers posted 18 points and ten rebounds, for his second career double-double.{{cite web|title=No. 25 Michigan beats Nebraska 82-58 with Beilein on hand|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166262|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 5, 2020|access-date=March 5, 2020}}{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|title=Wolverines Rout Nebraska for Senior Day Win|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2020/3/5/mens-basketball-wolverines-rout-nebraska-for-senior-day-win.aspx|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=March 5, 2020|access-date=March 5, 2020}} At the close of the regular season, Livers was named honorable mention [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] by the media.{{cite press release|title=Big Ten Unveils Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN|url=https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200309231733/https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 9, 2020|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]|date=March 9, 2020|access-date=March 9, 2020}} Livers started 21 games and averaged 12.9 points per game while shooting 40 percent from behind the arc. He missed only two free-throws the entire season, making 44-for-46 (.957) from the line.{{cite web|title=Isaiah Livers announces return to Michigan basketball for 2020-21|url=https://wolverineswire.usatoday.com/2020/07/17/michigan-basketball-isaiah-livers-to-return-for-senior-season/|website=WolverinesWire.USAToday.com|date=July 17, 2020|access-date=July 17, 2020}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], but did not hire an agent and left the door open to return for his senior season.{{cite news|first=Andrew|last=Kahn|title=Michigan junior Isaiah Livers declares for NBA draft|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2020/03/michigan-junior-isaiah-livers-declares-for-nba-draft.html|work=MLive.com|date=March 30, 2020|access-date=March 31, 2020}} On July 17, 2020, Livers announced that he would return to Michigan for his senior season.{{cite web|first=Orion|last=Sang|title=Michigan basketball gets big boost with Isaiah Livers returning for his senior year|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/07/17/michigan-basketball-isaiah-livers-nba-draft/5459872002/|work=Detroit Free Press|date=July 17, 2020|access-date=July 17, 2020}} === Senior season (2020–2021) === During his senior season, Livers posted 16 double-figure games with a team-high five 20+ point games, and averaged 13.9 points per game. Livers made a team-high 50 three-pointers, reaching 50+ in a season for the second time in his career. He averaged a career-best 6.2 rebounds and 2.0 assists, and he added a pair of double-doubles. Following the season, he was named second-team All-Big Ten by the coaches and media.{{cite web|title=2020-21 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|url=https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/9/general-2020-21-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309180252/https://bigten.org/news/2021/3/9/general-2020-21-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 9, 2021|website=BigTen.org|date=March 9, 2021|access-date=March 9, 2021}}{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|title=Dickinson, Howard Headline Big Ten Awards as Top Freshman, Coach|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/9/mens-basketball-dickinson-howard-headline-big-ten-awards-as-top-freshman-coach.aspx|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=March 9, 2021|access-date=March 9, 2021}} On March 13, 2021, Livers suffered a stress injury to his right foot during a quarterfinal game against [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]] in the [[2021 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2021 Big Ten tournament]], which sidelined him indefinitely.{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|title=Livers Out Indefinitely with Stress Injury to Right Foot|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/3/13/mens-basketball-livers-out-indefinitely-with-stress-injury-to-right-foot.aspx|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=March 13, 2021|access-date=March 13, 2021}} On April 2, 2021, Livers underwent successful surgery on his foot, with his recovery time expected to be a minimum of six months.{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|title=Livers Undergoes Successful Surgery on Right Foot|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2021/4/2/mens-basketball-livers-undergoes-successful-surgery-on-right-foot.aspx|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=April 2, 2021|access-date=April 2, 2021}} On April 16, 2021, Livers declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=Michigan guard Isaiah Livers declares for NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/news/michigan-guard-isaiah-livers-declares-for-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=April 16, 2021|access-date=April 16, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Detroit Pistons (2021–2024)=== Livers was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 42nd pick by his hometown team the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite news|first=Ryan|last=Zuke|title=NBA Draft 2021: Detroit Pistons select Michigan’s Isaiah Livers in second
